source.title: Revenge of Monosemanticity: Neuron Specialization as a New Form of Feature Learning in MLPs
source.authors: Amirhesam Abedsoltan; Enric Boix-Adserà; Fivos Kalogiannis; M. Belkin

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses language-model monosemanticity but its own results concern synthetic MLPs and cluster-selective activation, not named semantic jobs or any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures weight alignment with cluster-specific spans and activation energy on the corresponding cluster in synthetic regression MLPs. These results concern neuron specialization and cluster selectivity, but do not measure whether explanations name a neuron's job or test the listed model-interpretability claims.
record.test_reason: The study trains one-hidden-layer MLPs on synthetic Gaussian-mixture regression. It scores neurons by weight alignment with a cluster's mean/predictive span and by cluster-selective activation energy. It does not audit neurons in a language or vision model, write or score explanations, or build attribution graphs, so no version's behaviour is measured. Its only contact with the claim is a prior-work paragraph citing Bills et al. (an original source) and other work on LM monosemanticity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct but incomplete. The authors conclude that MLPs on clustered data learn many local low-dimensional representations through neuron specialization, not one global subspace, and that many specialized neurons are monosemantic (cluster-selective). They add two further results. First, specialization gives MLPs a sample-efficiency advantage over global kernel methods and RFM, shown empirically and proven polynomial vs super-polynomial in K. Second, gated activations improve sample complexity. Theorem 1 proves that small-initialized ReLU neurons specialize.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic Gaussian-mixture regression MLP experiments; measures geometric alignment and cluster-specific activation energy rather than explaining neuron activations with natural-language job descriptions or testing explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by activation type: the reported specialization rates and monosemanticity measures differ across ReLU, GELU, ReGLU, and SwiGLU.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic clustered-regression MLPs (width 4096), a large share of active neurons align with one cluster's span (Sj≥0.9: 15.7–95.2% depending on activation and setting), against a near-zero random-orientation null. Among specialized neurons, cluster-selective activation depends strongly on activation type. ReGLU is highest (mean Mj 0.945–0.996; 95.6–100% with Mj>1/2). GELU and SwiGLU are lower (mean Mj 0.44–0.72). The authors state specialization does not guarantee monosemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In shallow MLPs trained on clustered data, neurons specialize to single clusters well above chance. How exclusively they fire on that cluster depends on the activation function, with gated ReGLU most selective. This is a geometric and activation-energy proxy, not a measure of explainable jobs.

record.problems: The experiments use synthetic, low-dimensional clustered regression settings rather than language models. Their geometric and cluster-energy scores do not test whether a natural-language explanation captures a neuron's job or predicts activation on held-out examples. The table summaries use three runs.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares (about 90/7/2–4%). No language model is studied.
Shares across language models, dense and MoE, up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization.
Interpretable-neuron share in real vision/language models as tools and architectures improve. Activation-type differences in synthetic MLPs use geometric/energy proxies, not interpretability shares.
Neuron-based attribution graphs versus replacement models.
Held-out prediction of activation from explanations built on activating examples.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper mentions LM monosemanticity and cites Bills et al. only in one prior-work paragraph, without engaging any version. The activation-dependence of monosemanticity loosely echoes V4's architecture theme. It is not linked, because the setting (synthetic regression MLPs) and measures (weight alignment, activation energy) differ from interpretable-neuron shares in real models. Random-orientation rows are legitimate controls but bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B audit shares and neuron-pole job explanations.
Language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, and scale up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, and recursive generalization.
Vision-model interpretability estimates and the proposed architecture, regularization, and tool effects.
Attribution graphs using a model's neurons versus replacement models and reconstruction error.
Held-out prediction tests of neuron explanations based on activating examples.
Automated neuron-explanation scores from activation simulation on new text.
